metadata.title: feat(rate-limiter): pluggable algorithms, Redis token bucket, and load test harness
metadata.author: gandhipratik203

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #[rate-limiter-algorithms-issue]

---

## 📝 Summary

This PR extends the rate limiter plugin with a **pluggable algorithm strategy**, a **Redis backend for token bucket**, and a **load test harness** for benchmarking algorithm behaviour at scale.

### Problem Statement
The original rate limiter used a single fixed-window counting strategy. This meant:
- **No burst absorption** — short client spikes were rejected immediately
- **Boundary burst exposure** — up to 2× the configured limit could slip through at window resets
- **Silent under-enforcement in multi-instance deployments** — `token_bucket` stored state in process memory, so 3 gateway instances behind a load balancer effectively tripled the configured limit
- **No load test coverage** for multi-instance correctness or Redis memory divergence across algorithms

### Solution
- **Three selectable algorithms** via `algorithm:` in plugin config — `fixed_window`, `sliding_window`, `token_bucket`
- **Redis backend for `token_bucket`** — atomic Lua script stores `{tokens, last_refill}` per key, one round-trip per check, true cluster-wide enforcement across all gateway instances
- **Algorithm comparison load test** — live gateway CPU/memory + Redis memory timeline, one run per algorithm
- **Scale divergence load test** — 100 unique users, each with their own Redis key, shows memory growth rate diverging by algorithm at scale

### Key Components
- **`rate_limiter.py`** — `AlgorithmBackend` strategy pattern; `FixedWindowBackend`, `SlidingWindowBackend`, `TokenBucketBackend` (memory + Redis); atomic Lua scripts for all three Redis paths
- **`locustfile_rate_limiter_algorithms.py`** — single-user algorithm comparison with docker stats + Redis memory polling
- **`locustfile_rate_limiter_scale.py`** — N-user scale test showing Redis memory divergence (fixed_window O(N) vs sliding_window O(N×W))
- **`Makefile`** — `benchmark-rate-limiter-algorithms` and `benchmark-rate-limiter-scale` targets
- **`README.md`** — updated with algorithm trade-off table, Redis backend docs, and per-algorithm examples

## 📓 Notes
`token_bucket` with `backend: redis` stores `{tokens, last_refill}` per key using an atomic Lua script — one round-trip per check, no race condition. All three algorithms support both `memory` and `redis` backends. The `redis_fallback: true` option falls back to in-process memory if Redis is unavailable, so no requests are blocked due to Redis downtime.

test(rate-limiter): harden rate limiter plugin — gaps #1-#8

Closes #3740

## What changed

### Plugin fixes (plugins/rate_limiter/rate_limiter.py)
- Config validation at __init__: _validate_config() parses all rate
  strings at startup — bad config raises immediately, not mid-request
- Graceful degradation: both hooks wrapped in try/except; unexpected
  errors are logged and the request is allowed through (permissive)
- prompt_pre_fetch now enforces by_tool limits using prompt_id as key
- MemoryBackend: asyncio.Lock makes counter increments atomic
- MemoryBackend: background TTL sweep evicts expired windows (0.5s interval)
- RedisBackend: atomic INCR+EXPIRE via Lua script; shared state across
  all gateway instances; native TTL expiry; falls back to memory on error

### Test additions (tests/unit/.../test_rate_limiter.py)
- Gap tests: 4 xfail -> pass (shared state, eviction, prompt by_tool,
  graceful degradation); 1 xfail remains (fixed window burst, deferred)
- Edge case tests: malformed/unsupported config raises at init (not
  request time); runtime errors degrade gracefully via mock injection
- Redis backend test uses injected FakeRedis — no live server required

### Config changes
- plugins/config.yaml: RateLimiterPlugin enabled with enforce mode
- tests/performance/plugins/config.yaml: RateLimiterPlugin set to
  permissive for inclusion in cProfile benchmark runs

commits.message:
chore(config): enable Redis backend for RateLimiterPlugin in plugins/config.yaml

Switch the default stack config from in-memory to Redis-backed rate limiting.
This ensures the 30/m per-user limit is enforced as a true shared limit across
all gateway instances rather than 30/m per process.

Validated via Redis MONITOR: all 3 gateway instances atomically increment the
same rl:user:<id>:60 counter via the Lua INCR+EXPIRE script.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): add benchmark-rate-limiter load test for multi-instance correctness

Adds locustfile_rate_limiter.py and a make benchmark-rate-limiter target to
demonstrate the multi-instance rate limit enforcement gap and its fix.

The test sends 1 req/s (60 req/min = 2x the 30/m limit) through 3 gateway
instances. With a memory backend each instance only sees ~20 req/min and
never fires the limiter (~0% failures). With the Redis backend the shared
counter reaches 30/min and blocks ~50% of requests — clearly showing the fix
works across instances.

Expected results:
  Memory backend:  ~0% blocked  (each instance sees 20 req/min < 30/m limit)
  Redis backend:  ~50% blocked  (shared counter: 60 req/min > 30/m limit)

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

test(rate-limiter): add hardening tests, bypass resistance, PII fix, and updated docs

- Add 22 new unit tests (70 passed total, 4 xfailed):
  - Permissive vs enforce mode through PluginExecutor
  - Redis fallback: memory takeover when Redis is down, limit still enforced, no-fallback graceful degradation
  - Cross-tenant isolation: independent counters, no counter bleed between tenants
  - Header accuracy: Retry-After bounds, X-RateLimit-Reset future/consistency, Remaining decrement
  - Bypass resistance: None/whitespace user identity, tool name case sensitivity and whitespace (documented as xfail gaps)
  - PII: violation description must not contain user or tenant identifiers

- Fix PII leak in violation description: remove user/tenant from description string
  in both prompt_pre_fetch and tool_pre_invoke — identifiers appeared in log output
  via permissive-mode manager warning and enforce-mode PluginViolationError message

- Rewrite plugins/rate_limiter/README.md: was describing the old pre-fix
  implementation (in-memory only, no Redis, Redis as TODO). Now documents
  both backends, full config reference, response headers, examples, and
  accurate limitations table

- Update plugin-manifest.yaml description to reflect Redis backend support

Closes #3740

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

commits.message:
feat(rate-limiter): pluggable algorithm strategy — fixed window, sliding window, token bucket

Adds a strategy pattern for rate counting algorithms, selectable via
`algorithm:` in plugin config. All three are fully tested (84 pass, 4 xfail).

Algorithms:
- fixed_window (default): existing fixed-window counter; unchanged behaviour
- sliding_window: per-key timestamp log, no boundary burst; Redis-native
  via ZADD+ZREMRANGEBYSCORE+ZCARD+EXPIRE Lua script
- token_bucket: refills at steady rate, allows short bursts up to capacity;
  memory-only (falls back from Redis with a warning)

Implementation:
- Each algorithm is a small class (allow/sweep) — MemoryBackend delegates
  all counting to the injected algorithm instance
- RedisBackend selects between _LUA_FIXED and _LUA_SLIDING based on algorithm
- Per-instance backends (module-level singleton removed); asyncio.Lock and
  sweep task are per-backend, not global
- RateLimiterConfig gets algorithm field (validated at __init__)
- PII removed from violation description (user/tenant no longer logged)

Tests: 14 new algorithm tests covering enforcement, burst behaviour, header
accuracy, Redis fallback, and instance isolation. All bypass-resistance xfails
and prior xfails remain documented.

README: documents algorithm field, comparison table, per-algorithm notes,
Redis Lua scripts, two new examples, updated limitations table.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

feat(rate-limiter): pluggable algorithms, Redis backend, and load test harness

- Add sliding_window and token_bucket algorithms alongside fixed_window;
  selection via algorithm config field
- Add Redis backend with atomic Lua scripts for all three algorithms —
  one round-trip per check, no race conditions
- Fix Lua sliding window bugs: check-before-ZADD so blocked requests do
  not inflate the sorted set; unique member per entry to prevent timestamp
  collisions
- Normalise user, tenant, and tool identities (.strip().lower()) for
  consistent key generation across both hooks
- Align RedisBackend token-bucket reset_timestamp with memory backend;
  compute time_to_full from remaining tokens
- Pre-compute normalised by_tool dict once at init (_normalised_by_tool)
- Harden _parse_rate with maxsplit=1 and clear error messages
- Remove dead _store/_allow module-level stubs
- Add load test harnesses: algorithm comparison and Redis/memory scale tests
- Add comprehensive unit and integration test coverage for all algorithms,
  backends, hooks, and edge cases

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
